newsitem.title: USA: Banks need an image change, new ABA chief says.
newsitem.headline: Banks need an image change, new ABA chief says.

text.p: The banking industry suffers from an image problem and the new head of the American Bankers Association says he's going to try for a makeover.
"Banks don't get much respect. As a banker I'm tired of that," Walter Dods, the new president of the trade association, said at the group's convention, which ends Tuesday.
The negative image stems from such factors as fees and it is blocking the industry's political goals, he said.

"I hope to get the ball rolling next year on a campaign to change America's perception of banks. Why? because our image is hurting us," Dods said. "A business with more popular support, or at least less animosity, wouldn't be so easy a target for cheap shots," he added.

Dods, chairman and chief executive officer of First Hawaiian Inc. and its main subsidiary First Hawaiian Bank, has a background in marketing. Consumers need to understand the services they receive for the bank fees charged, he said.
"It is a realistic goal to give Americans a better appreciation for the role banks play in our nation's economy," he said.
Dods later said his comments did not mean banks should do away with the fees, but rather the industry needed to explain to consumers the value received.
